text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- UDF junior coalition party leader Francois Leotard details in an interview the ruling coalition's platform unveiled last week, which includes plans for further tax cuts, aims to suppress state budget deficit within four to five years.
-- New car registrations in France fell 22.5 percent since January 1997.

-- Budget minister Alain Lamassoure says in an interview the ruling coalition aims to get the state's operational budget to breakeven point by the year 2000. Adds Finance Minister Jean Arthuis plans to distinguish in the 1998 budget between state operational spending and state spending on investment and that rebalancing the former was a priority.
-- Economists polled by the newspaper bet on delays in monetary union with Germany.

-- A Sofres poll for Le Figaro sees the ruling conservative coalition winning 291 seats in the upcoming parliamentary election, while 41 percent of the people polled call for a Socialist victory, and 35 percent remain undecided.
-- Strike to carry on for two days at Air France Europe against terms of a merger with Air France.

-- 49 percent of people polled by Ifop for Liberation think the ruling majority's target of switching to a single European currency by January 1, 1999 is "rather irrealistic", and 51 percent think the same of planned tax cuts linked to state savings.
-- Daimler Benz Aerospace AG wants to team up with the winning bidder for defense-electronics group Thomson-CSF, to encourage integration among European defense companies.
